narrative: Material PL2__M13FA8BE shows a statistically significant upward demand trend across 218 working days, with daily demand rising from ~1,100 to ~2,700 units. Lead times are extremely short (mean 0.28 days) but highly variable (CV 1.37), making lead-time uncertainty the dominant buffer driver at 63.8% of total variance. The (r,Q) policy is selected because fixed-batch ordering aligns with the MOQ constraint and the continuous-review trigger is straightforward given short, observable lead times. The current SAP safety stock of 17,491 units is 16x the analytically derived requirement, representing a significant overstock that can be safely reduced to 1,062 units while maintaining 95% service level.
warnings: Upward demand trend detected — reorder point and safety stock should be reviewed quarterly.
Lead time estimate based on only 10 observations — monitor with additional delivery data.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The material has a MOQ of 17,491 which makes fixed-batch ordering natural. Lead times are short and directly observable, enabling a continuous-review trigger without requiring periodic-review overhead. The (r,Q) model minimises total ordering and holding costs via EOQ while using the reorder point to absorb lead-time and demand uncertainty at the 95% service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: EOQ of 26,232 comfortably exceeds MOQ of 17,491 so no MOQ binding constraint. Total inventory at replenishment (27,294 units) is 59% below the 66,698-unit storage cap — no capacity binding. However, the upward demand trend means ROP will underestimate true demand-during-lead-time if not refreshed; this creates a progressive service degradation risk without quarterly recalibration.
